config.title: Recursive TreeView

intro.title: Recursive TreeView
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TreeView component that displays a nested folder structure. You will learn how to use recursion in React to render components that call themselves to handle deeply nested data. The main technologies involved are React components, TypeScript interfaces for type safety, and recursive function calls. By the end, you will understand how to map over data and conditionally render child components to create a dynamic, expandable tree interface.
intro.usecase: The recursive TreeView pattern is essential for displaying hierarchical data in modern applications. You'll see it in file explorers like VS Code's sidebar, where folders contain nested files and subfolders. It's also used in navigation menus for complex dashboards, organizational charts in HR software, and category filters in e-commerce sites. As a developer, implementing this pattern efficiently allows users to intuitively browse and interact with deeply nested structures.

objectives: Construct a recursive TypeScript interface to define tree node data structures
Implement a React component that renders tree nodes recursively
Initialize and manage component state to control node expansion and collapse
Bind click handlers to toggle node visibility within the recursive tree
Configure conditional rendering logic to display nested child nodes
Apply TypeScript type safety to recursive component props and state
Manipulate tree data structures to demonstrate recursive rendering patterns

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define TreeNode interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named TreeNode with three properties: id (string), label (string), and children (array of TreeNode objects).
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Remember that children should be an array of TreeNode objects to allow recursion.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define TreeNode interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TreeNode interface is defined with the correct properties, enabling type-safe tree node data structures.
successCriteria: TreeNode interface exists with id: string, label: string, and children: TreeNode[] properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you have all three properties: id (string), label (string), and children (array of TreeNode objects).
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode interface is missing or incomplete. Make sure to define an interface with id: string, label: string, and children: TreeNode[].

steps.title: Create TreeView component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TreeView that accepts a prop called 'nodes' typed as TreeNode[] and returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name TreeView, include a parameter for nodes with the correct type annotation, and return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TreeView component is defined with proper TypeScript typing for its nodes prop.
successCriteria: TreeView is a functional component that accepts a prop named 'nodes' of type TreeNode[] and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component accepts a 'nodes' prop typed as TreeNode[] and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the component definition: it should be named TreeView, take a 'nodes' prop of type TreeNode[], and return null.

steps.title: Add expanded state to TreeNodeItem
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, use the useState hook to declare a state variable named 'isExpanded' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the initial argument and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component will have an 'isExpanded' state variable initialized to false, ready to track the node's expanded/collapsed status.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called inside TreeNodeItem, declaring a state variable named 'isExpanded' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState inside the TreeNodeItem component and naming the variable 'isExpanded' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNodeItem component doesn't yet have the required state. Add a useState call inside it to create an 'isExpanded' variable initialized to false.

steps.title: Define toggle handler
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, define a function named toggleExpanded that toggles the expanded state value.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setExpanded with the opposite of the current expanded value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component will have a toggleExpanded function that flips the expanded state when called.
successCriteria: A toggleExpanded function is defined inside TreeNodeItem that toggles the expanded state using setExpanded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure toggleExpanded is a function that calls setExpanded with the opposite of the current expanded value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleExpanded function is missing or doesn't properly toggle the state. Check that it's defined inside TreeNodeItem and uses setExpanded.

steps.title: Render node label and toggle button
steps.instruction: In the TreeNodeItem component's return statement, replace the null with JSX that displays the node's label and a toggle button for expand/collapse.
steps.hint: Return a <div> containing a <span> with the node's label and a <button> that says 'Toggle'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component now returns a <div> with a <span> showing the node's label and a <button> with the text 'Toggle'.
successCriteria: The TreeNodeItem component returns JSX containing a <span> with {node.label} and a <button> with the text 'Toggle'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your JSX includes both the node label in a <span> and a <button> with 'Toggle' text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNodeItem component should return JSX with a <span> displaying the node's label and a <button> with 'Toggle' text.

steps.title: Wire toggle button to handler
steps.instruction: In the TreeNodeItem component, add an onClick event to the toggle button that calls the toggleExpanded handler function.
steps.hint: Add onClick={toggleExpanded} to the button element that renders the + or - symbol.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggle button will now respond to clicks, changing the expanded state when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has an onClick attribute set to toggleExpanded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button's onClick attribute is set to toggleExpanded.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still needs an onClick handler. Add onClick={toggleExpanded} to the button element.

steps.title: Add recursive rendering of children
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, after the button, conditionally render the node's children when expanded is true. Use the TreeView component to render the children array.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&) to conditionally render. If expanded and node.children exists, render <TreeView nodes={node.children} />.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component will recursively render child nodes when the toggle button is clicked and expanded becomes true.
successCriteria: The TreeNodeItem component conditionally renders <TreeView nodes={node.children} /> when expanded is true and node.children exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct condition and rendering the TreeView component with the children array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The recursive rendering isn't implemented correctly. Check that you're conditionally rendering based on the expanded state and passing node.children to TreeView.

steps.title: Complete TreeView component rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeView component, map through the nodes prop and render a TreeNodeItem component for each root node.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the nodes array. For each node, return a TreeNodeItem component with the node prop set to the current node.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeView component will now render all root nodes using the TreeNodeItem component.
successCriteria: TreeView maps through nodes prop and returns TreeNodeItem components for each node.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping through the nodes prop and returning a TreeNodeItem for each node.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeView component still returns null. You need to map through the nodes prop and render TreeNodeItem components.

steps.title: Create sample tree data
steps.instruction: Define a constant named 'sampleTreeData' that contains an array of TreeNode objects to test the TreeView component.
steps.hint: Create a const variable with type TreeNode[] and initialize it with an array of objects that have 'label' and optional 'children' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sampleTreeData constant is created with a hierarchical structure that matches the TreeNode interface.
successCriteria: sampleTreeData is defined as a const variable with type TreeNode[], containing at least one root node with nested children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure sampleTreeData is a const array that properly follows the TreeNode interface structure with label and optional children properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample data wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a constant named sampleTreeData that contains an array of TreeNode objects.

steps.title: Export and use TreeView with sample data
steps.instruction: Export the TreeView component and render it with the sample tree data inside the component's return statement.
steps.hint: First, add the export keyword before the TreeView function. Then, in the TreeView component's return statement, map through the nodes prop and render a TreeNodeItem for each node.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeView component is exported and renders the sample tree data with expandable/collapsible nodes.
successCriteria: TreeView component is exported and correctly maps through the nodes prop to render TreeNodeItem components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the export keyword before TreeView and updated its return statement to map through the nodes prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeView component isn't properly exported or doesn't render the sample data. Check that you've added 'export default TreeView' and updated the return statement.
